body:
PROCEDURE: waits and handoffs, shared by Engram and TermAl. Shared changes go through both coordinators. TermAl mirrors this text verbatim in its own store. Source: Greg via Advisor #1009: "for every handoff/wait, who owns it, what starts next, the named dependency/result, where it is recorded, who/what sends the wake, and the recovery route if delivery fails". Current operating guidance; prior concurrence and incident history remain in work notes and revisions. This is a working procedure, not automation; it adds no authority.

RULE. Before ending a turn with a dependency outstanding, write a WAIT line and notify its wake owner. A turn boundary, a future credit line or "someone will notice" is not a wake sender. For a boundary-only wait, send the coordinator a final "READY: <exact dependency>"; the coordinator sends the continuation immediately on receipt, even while you're still active. BY is a human coordination deadline, not a host timer. If the recovery owner has no independent wake, write "RECOVERY GAP".

WAIT LINE: a status note on the held item; a mailbox message to the coordinator if no claim is held or the item is already done.
- OWNER: the waiting session.
- ON: the exact dependency identity: run id and directory, delegation and fan-in wait ids, mailbox plus sender plus request message id, or item, run and claim.
- WAKE: the sender and route.
- NEXT: the first action on waking.
- BY: absolute UTC, an estimate agreed by its owner. Without a better estimate, use evaluator 10 min, review pair 20 min, full gate 25 min, focused check 5 min.
- RECOVERY: a named session plus absolute UTC, and what it does.
The note documents the wait; it registers no automatic wake. A status or WAIT note is not a check and does not stale an evaluation.

STANDARD WAITS
1a GATE RESULT. ON: run id, directory, fingerprint. For indexed same-project runs, register termal_resume_after_test_runs and end the turn; TermAl wakes with bounded results. No operator agent, model polling or log stream. Otherwise use launcher --notify and coordinator relay. Recovery reads the existing run on a real wake; never rerun for delivery. Deliver FAIL, UNKNOWN and fingerprint mismatch too. No owner commands or edits during a carried run.
1b HOST CREDIT, after a gate or focused check. ON: the same run plus work, run and claim, awaiting the host verification record or its refusal. A credit line is not a wake: send READY, and the coordinator continues you. NEXT: read the recorded evidence; request evaluation only in a later turn, and only once the record exists. Passing output alone is not credit. If credit stays absent after a relay, report that exact state; it is a recording incident with an owner, not a relay loop. Under the TermAl host (both projects): make no file edits anywhere in the session and run no non-read command in that worktree until the host credit record or its refusal has landed; writes after the launcher finishes still count until the host settles. Then the owner may use its worktree again; the credit record is also needed before requesting evaluation. This applies only to runs the host records as checks: a detached full gate, or a foreground check whose command the host recognises. A detached focused run, or a custom script, is never recorded; there is no credit record to wait for, the 1a completion ends the wait, and such a run earns no credit.
2 GATE QUEUE / LAUNCH NOW. ON: the queued slot, item, prepared root and fingerprint, and the command. WAKE: the coordinator's LAUNCH NOW, sent only after READY. NEXT: that one command, then end under the carried-gate rules. All notes and fixes come before launch. A stale slot goes back to the coordinator.
3 PAIR OR EVALUATOR. ON: both review delegation ids, or the evaluator delegation and attempt, plus the returned fan-in wait id. WAKE: TermAl fan-in to the parent; a failed registration is no fan-in. NEXT: fetch the actual results. RECOVERY: the coordinator at BY+15 sends a mailbox continuation; the parent recovers existing results and never respawns because a delivery failed. A held or attention-required child, or an evaluation for a different attempt or basis, is not a clean result.
4 COORDINATOR RULING, CONCURRENCE OR WINDOW. ON: item, proposed text and request message id. WAKE: the coordinator's reply. An answer of "I need X" replaces the wait with X, its owner and a new BY.
5 PEER REPLY. ON: mailbox, expected sender and request id; a later unrelated message is not the reply. A sleeping waiter cannot re-ping itself, so RECOVERY names an independently waking session or says GAP.
6 FOCUS OR NAMING BINDING. Send "READY: binding only" with the exact item and claim; the coordinator replies at once. NEXT: verify the binding took effect, then retry only the refused operation; never edit or test in the naming turn to work around it. A repeated 409 is diagnosed, not worked around. Focus is a pointer, not ownership.
7 LANDING. The holder owns it until the integration owner accepts; Engram's coder is its own integration owner. ON: commit, base, gate run, pair ids and completion evidence. Engram: install with a backup BEFORE the push. TermAl: the integration owner pushes, verifies the remote, then installs with a backup outside any gate window. In both, the pre-push notice is not a wait. In TermAl only the assigned integration owner pushes; other sessions hand off. The coordinator verifies, then sends "master is X" to every coder waiting on it. RECOVERY: ask the owner for its exact stage, and re-read the actual state before any retry.
8 RESTART (TermAl host). OWNER: both coordinators; Merger installs Engram. Follow rules-install-and-cutover: Greg's window -> INSTALL NOW -> verified INSTALLED -> RESTART NOW via Advisor. Lead restart notices with HOLD until release. Name TermAl main commit; Greg rebuilds it. No restart ~15 min after agreed time: restore Engram, withdraw release. Verify no old consumers before cutover/resume. Recover existing receipts on wake; no timer.
9 GREG DECISION, RESUME OR PROVIDER PARK. ON: the exact question and Advisor request id, or the parked session and its refusal. WAKE: the Advisor relaying Greg's actual word or Resume. BY: the next agreed status point. Silence never approves. Credit exhaustion is an external limit, not something to retry.

COORDINATOR DUTIES, on each actual wake: process the mailboxes; inspect assigned waits and sessions; act on overdue or missing WAIT lines, each wake naming the dependency and the next action. No wake storms for parked sessions. A send receipt proves the message was stored, not that the session was admitted or ran; provider, Stop or approval blocks stay visible. Recovery must not form an all-asleep cycle: name the waking checker, or state GAP. The Advisor is NOT the coordinator's recovery owner (Greg DIRECT 2026-10-25): the coordinator's own recovery is the other project's coordinator where both have agreed it for a named wait; otherwise it is stated as RECOVERY GAP. Advisor only relays information to/from project coordinators; see rules-roles-and-council.

KNOWN GAP: coordination BY deadlines have no timer. A BY is checked only when its checker is actually woken. Automation (w-4e75a5319cde, w-3123ce57e780; TermAl w-5043851f081f, w-15acfd0087c2) stays parked until Greg's word.

MUTUAL COORDINATOR RECOVERY. For each agreed named wait, record the other coordinator, deadline, wake route and handback. Recovery requires an owner who can execute; status=active or a send receipt alone does not prove that. If both coordinators are unavailable, record RECOVERY GAP and route it to the existing council to recover a named available AUTHORIZED owner who accepts the bounded duty. A new deputy needs recorded authority and acceptance for the affected waits; this clause grants no blanket appointment or slot power. Preserve existing claims, resource grants, STOP and restart boundaries. Advisor remains relay-only; architects do not become schedulers. Recover the existing request/result, not a duplicate run. Hand back explicitly when the regular owner resumes. A deadline still creates no timer; it is checked only when the recovery owner is woken.
